items.title: Bank of England raises interest rates to 4%, first rise since 2023
items.why: The Bank of England raised its main rate from 3.75% to 4% on Thursday, by eight votes to one; one member wanted 4.25%. It blames higher fuel costs from the Iran war and expects UK inflation, 3.5% in September, to reach about 5% by mid-2027.
items.matters: Borrowers on variable and tracker mortgages will pay more; the Bank says further rises are possible but not certain.

items.title: Saudi-led coalition says it shot down Houthi missile fired towards Medina
items.why: The Saudi-led coalition in Yemen says its air defences destroyed a ballistic missile fired by Yemen's Houthis at Saudi Arabia's Medina region on Thursday. Saudi civil defence had earlier warned of danger near the Red Sea port of Yanbu. No damage or casualties have been reported.
items.matters: Yanbu is where a pipeline lets Saudi oil avoid the Strait of Hormuz.

items.title: Cristiano Ronaldo retires from international football with Portugal
items.why: Cristiano Ronaldo, 41, announced on social media on Thursday that he is retiring from Portugal's national team after 23 years. He leaves with men's international records of 234 appearances and 146 goals, and won Euro 2016 and two Nations League titles.
items.matters: It follows a dispute with coach Jorge Jesus; Ronaldo will keep playing for Al Nassr in Saudi Arabia.

items.title: French unions and students strike and march over pay and living costs
items.why: France's main unions held nationwide strikes and marches on Thursday, demanding higher wages and better public services, joined by school students. The CGT union says more than 250,000 people marched in 73 cities by lunchtime. The Eiffel Tower closed and police used tear gas in Lyon.
items.matters: It follows earlier protests in France over living costs, public services and education.

items.title: Hong Kong activist Joshua Wong jailed for 10 more years
items.why: Hong Kong's High Court sentenced pro-democracy activist Joshua Wong, 30, to 10 years in prison on Thursday for conspiring to collude with foreign forces under the national security law. He had pleaded guilty in September and was due for release in January.
items.matters: The US consulate and rights groups condemned the sentence; China told other countries not to interfere in Hong Kong's courts.

items.title: Alan Jones, 1980 Formula One world champion, dies aged 80
items.why: Australian racing driver Alan Jones, who won the 1980 Formula One world title with Williams, has died aged 80 after a short illness, his wife said on Thursday. He won 12 Grands Prix and later commentated on F1 for Australian television.
items.matters: He and Jack Brabham are the only Australians to have won the Formula One drivers' title.

items.title: South Korea plans naval mission near the Strait of Hormuz
items.why: South Korea's government on Thursday backed a plan to extend its Gulf of Aden anti-piracy unit's area to waters off Oman, near the Strait of Hormuz, adding a patrol plane and mine-clearing teams. It still needs cabinet and parliamentary approval. Seoul says the mission is non-combat.
items.matters: About a fifth of the world's oil normally passes through the strait; Iran has warned Seoul against the deployment.

items.title: Pilot whales die in mass stranding on New Zealand's North Island
items.why: Dozens of pilot whales stranded at Ngawi, near Cape Palliser at the southern tip of New Zealand's North Island, on Thursday. The conservation department counted about 20 on the beach and locals reported up to 50. Rescuers refloated two, but the last survivors died, Project Jonah says.
items.matters: The conservation department says the area has not had a mass stranding since the 1990s; the cause is not yet known.

items.title: Australian department store David Jones goes into voluntary administration
items.why: David Jones, Australia's 188-year-old department store chain, went into voluntary administration on Thursday after rent talks with landlords including Westfield's owner broke down. Its 38 stores and website keep trading while receivers review the business.
items.matters: Receivers blame rising costs and an outdated store network; news on store closures and jobs is expected this week.

items.title: Como win 9-1 at Lens as Fenerbahce end Liverpool's perfect run
items.why: Como beat Lens 9-1 in the Champions League on Wednesday, equalling the competition's biggest winning margin. Fenerbahce beat Liverpool 3-2 in Istanbul, ending their perfect record in the competition, and Real Madrid won 3-2 at AEK Athens with a stoppage-time goal.
items.matters: Arsenal and Manchester City also won, beating Slavia Prague 2-1 and RB Leipzig 3-2.

items.title: LIV Golf faces wind-down after investor drops relaunch plan, reports say
items.why: Private capital firm BC Partners has dropped plans to put up to $300 million into relaunching LIV Golf because too few players signed up, the Financial Times reports. The Saudi-funded tour filed for bankruptcy protection in New Jersey in September.
items.matters: South Australia's premier says LIV's event planned for Adelaide next March will not go ahead.

items.title: EU lawmakers back a softer 2035 emissions target for new cars
items.why: The European Parliament's environment committee voted 48 to 30 on Wednesday to cut the 2035 CO2 reduction target for new cars from 100% to 87.5%, with up to 7.5 points more covered by credits for low-carbon EU steel. The target for vans would fall to 80%.
items.matters: The current rule would in effect end sales of new petrol and diesel cars from 2035; the full Parliament votes in December.

items.changed: Updated: Swift re-entered over Indonesia on Wednesday.
items.title: NASA's Swift space telescope falls back to Earth over Indonesia
items.why: NASA's Swift observatory re-entered the atmosphere over North Sumatra, Indonesia, at 12:39 GMT on Wednesday, NASA and the US Space Force say. Launched in 2004 for a two-year study of gamma-ray bursts, it worked for 22 years. A commercial mission to raise its sinking orbit failed.
items.matters: Most of the 1.5-tonne craft burned up; NASA says some dense parts may have survived, and no damage has been reported.

items.title: WHO backs trials of two new vaccines against the Bundibugyo Ebola strain
items.why: WHO expert groups recommended adding two vaccines designed for the Bundibugyo strain, one from Oxford and the Serum Institute of India and one from Moderna, to a trial in the Democratic Republic of the Congo. The outbreak has killed more than 5,300 people since May, Africa CDC says.
items.matters: There is no approved vaccine or treatment for this strain; WHO expects trial results in early 2027.

items.title: Ethiopia and Sudan expel each other's consular staff
items.why: Ethiopia ordered six staff of Sudan's consulate in the border town of Asosa to leave within 48 hours, and Sudan closed Ethiopia's consulate in Gedaref in response, officials told Reuters, AP and AFP. Neither government gave a formal reason.
items.matters: Sudan accuses Ethiopia of letting Sudan's paramilitary RSF launch drone attacks from its soil; Ethiopia denies it.

items.title: Eurozone inflation rises to 4%, its highest in three years
items.why: Prices in the countries using the euro rose 4.0% in the year to October, up from 3.8% in September, Eurostat's first estimate shows. Energy prices were up 20.8%. Lithuania had the highest rate, 6.1%, and Malta the lowest, 2.3%.
items.matters: Markets now expect the European Central Bank to raise interest rates again in December, making borrowing dearer.

items.changed: Updated: Wall Street closed higher and oil fell below $95 (this replaces the separate oil story).
items.title: Wall Street jumps and oil falls after Democrats win Congress
items.why: The Dow Jones rose about 1,500 points, or 2.9%, on Wednesday after Democrats won both houses of Congress, AP reports, as investors expect fewer sudden policy changes. Brent crude fell 8.6% to about $95 a barrel on hopes the Iran war will wind down. Japan's Nikkei fell 1.4%.
items.matters: Cheaper oil feeds through to fuel, flight and food prices; Brent had been above $100 for nearly a month.

items.changed: Updated: with about 36% counted, the ANC leads the DA by about five points.
items.title: ANC narrowly leads DA as South African local votes are counted
items.why: With about 36% of votes counted by midday on Thursday, the ANC had about 32% and the Democratic Alliance 27%, Reuters reports. The DA leads in Cape Town, Johannesburg, Ekurhuleni and Nelson Mandela Bay, early counts show. Full results are expected on Sunday.
items.matters: The ANC won 46% in the last local elections in 2021; many councils may now need coalitions.

items.changed: Updated: Iran now says two more tankers and a tugboat caught fire on Thursday.
items.title: Iran says more tankers ablaze after mines near Strait of Hormuz
items.why: Iran's Revolutionary Guards said on Thursday that two more oil tankers and a tugboat caught fire on routes Iran bans near the Strait of Hormuz, one after hitting a mine, Reuters reports. On Wednesday the Guards said four tankers hit mines. Neither claim has been independently confirmed.
items.matters: Iran's supreme leader warned of a much wider war if attacks resume; Trump says he has no immediate plans for new strikes.

items.changed: Updated: Trump says the Iran war played a part; Alaska and Mississippi are still uncalled.
items.title: Democrats win control of US House and Senate
items.why: Democrats will control both the House of Representatives and the Senate after Tuesday's midterm elections, AP projects, with at least 54 Senate seats. Senate races in Alaska and Mississippi are still too close to call. Trump congratulated Democrats and said the Iran war was 'part of' the reason.
items.matters: From January, Democrats can block Trump's bills and open investigations; Michigan's Abdul El-Sayed will be the first Muslim US senator.

items.title: PSG beat Villarreal 6-0 as Barcelona and Bayern win in Champions League
items.why: Paris Saint-Germain won 6-0 away at Villarreal on 3 November, scoring four goals in the first 17 minutes, a competition record according to Opta. Barcelona beat Aston Villa 3-0, Bayern Munich won 2-0 at Atletico Madrid, and Manchester United came from two goals down to beat Roma 3-2.
items.matters: PSG lead the league phase with 12 points after four matches; the remaining matchday 4 games are played on Wednesday.

items.title: AMD's sales jump 45% as demand for AI chips nearly doubles
items.why: The US chipmaker AMD said third-quarter revenue rose 45% to $13.4 billion, with its data-centre business, which sells AI processors, up 97% to a record $8.5 billion. It expects about $17 billion in sales this quarter, and its shares rose about 8% after hours.
items.matters: It suggests companies are still spending heavily on AI computing, even as investors worry about whether that spending will pay off.

items.title: Spain's transport minister resigns after train crash that killed 69
items.why: Óscar Puente resigned on Tuesday, six days after a high-speed train hit a stationary train near Urda, south of Madrid, on 28 October. Spanish authorities give a provisional toll of 69 dead. Puente said a minister could not stay after two such serious crashes in a year.
items.matters: Investigators are examining why controllers let the train continue after a safety system failed, Euronews and Al Jazeera report.

items.title: Catalan writer Cristina Fernández Cubas wins the Cervantes Prize
items.why: Spain's culture minister, Ernest Urtasun, announced on 3 November that Cristina Fernández Cubas, born in 1945 in Arenys de Mar near Barcelona, has won the 2026 Cervantes Prize. The jury praised her short stories and fantastic fiction. The prize is worth €125,000.
items.matters: It is the top award for literature in Spanish, and she is only the seventh woman to win it since 1976.

items.title: Hoax bomb threats disrupt flights across Europe for a third day
items.why: At least 14 European flights received hoax bomb threats on Thursday, RTÉ and Euronews report, after similar threats on Monday and Tuesday. Three were diverted, including an Aer Lingus Dublin–Rome flight sent to a French air base. No explosives were found and all landed safely.
items.matters: No one has claimed responsibility; the EU says it is too early to say whether the threats are linked.
items.changed: Updated: a third and bigger wave of hoax threats hit at least 14 flights on Thursday.

items.title: Trump says US military aid to Israel will end this year
items.why: President Trump said on Tuesday that about $4 billion a year in US military funding for Israel will stop at the end of 2026, saying he and Prime Minister Netanyahu agreed it months ago. Netanyahu's office declined to comment. The current aid agreement runs until 2028.
items.matters: Israeli opposition figure Yair Golan says ending the aid would seriously harm Israel's security.

items.title: Indonesian president's chief of staff arrested over alleged phone tapping
items.why: Indonesian police have detained Listyo Sigit Prabowo, President Prabowo Subianto's chief of staff and a former national police chief, and two police generals on suspicion of illegally tapping the phones of the president, ministers and others. The president dismissed him on Wednesday.
items.matters: A presidential spokesman says it may amount to treason; officials say the motive is not yet known.

items.changed: Updated: host Germany says it is considering pulling out.
items.title: European teams say they will not play Russia at ice hockey worlds
items.why: Finland, Norway, Sweden, Denmark, Latvia and the Czech Republic say they will not play Russia at the 2027 men's world championship, after a sports court ruled on 30 October that Russia must be readmitted. Germany, the host, says it is considering withdrawing.
items.matters: Russia has been banned since invading Ukraine in 2022; the IIHF disagrees with the ruling but says it will comply.

items.changed: Updated: officials raised the death toll to 40, with 59 people still missing.
items.title: Ukraine says Russian strike on Zaporizhzhia aid point killed at least 40
items.why: Guided bombs hit a school used as an aid point in the village of Komyshuvakha, in south-eastern Ukraine, on Monday as residents gathered for aid, Ukrainian officials say. They now put the dead at 40, with 59 missing. Russia's defence ministry says it targeted Ukrainian military units.
items.matters: The US says Russian and Ukrainian delegations will meet for new talks in Abu Dhabi on 10 and 11 November.

items.changed: Updated: French blood banks say an attack on their cold stores was contained.
items.title: Cyberattacks on fridges spread across Europe and reach French blood banks
items.why: Hackers have tampered with refrigeration at supermarkets in at least 11 European countries, Al Jazeera reports, and at three French blood-bank cold stores overnight into Monday. France's health ministry says alarms worked and no blood was lost. No group has claimed responsibility.
items.matters: It follows a similar attack on refrigeration systems at hundreds of French supermarkets in October that forced stores to throw away food.

items.changed: Updated: the election result was certified and Herzog's consultations began.
items.title: Israel certifies election result as Herzog begins coalition talks
items.why: Israel's election committee certified the 27 October results on Wednesday, saying it found no evidence of fraud, after Netanyahu and his allies alleged, without evidence, that the vote was stolen. President Isaac Herzog is holding two days of consultations before choosing who will try to form a government.
items.matters: Netanyahu's bloc won 53 of 120 seats and Gadi Eisenkot's 48; Arab-led parties hold a record 19.
